sites.name: Northline
alreadyDoneWell: Unique titles, one H1 pattern, and canonicals look present on crawled pages.

findings.title: Publish a sitemap and point robots.txt at it
findings.what: Northline has no discoverable XML sitemap (checked common paths and robots.txt). robots.txt exists but has no Sitemap: line.
findings.why: A sitemap is how Google and AI crawlers learn the URL set quickly, especially after a redesign or launch.
findings.fix: Generate a sitemap (e.g. @astrojs/sitemap or equivalent), serve it at /sitemap-index.xml or /sitemap.xml, and add `Sitemap: <absolute-url>` to robots.txt. Submit it in Search Console after launch.

agentAction.notes: Ensure Sitemap: line uses the production absolute URL.

findings.title: Publish llms.txt
findings.why: A short, human-readable summary helps AI crawlers and assistants cite the right entity, especially when repositioning or launching.
findings.fix: Write public/llms.txt by hand: one paragraph on who the organisation is (legal name, place, founder, what it does and does not do), then links to key pages with one-line summaries.

artifacts.content:
# Northline

> Northline Advisory Ltd — replace this paragraph with: who you are, where,
> who founded you, what you do, and what you explicitly do not do.

## Pages
- [Northline | Advisory](https://staging.northline.example/): We help teams.

findings.title: Keep the staging host out of the index
findings.what: Staging host staging.northline.example appears indexable (no noindex meta and no X-Robots-Tag: noindex on the checked response).
findings.why: A canonical is a hint, not a rule. If anyone links to staging, Google may index it as a duplicate, and AI crawlers often ignore canonicals.
findings.fix: Send `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` only when the request host is the staging host (Worker rule or Cloudflare Transform Rule). Do not put noindex in HTML that ships to production.

findings.title: Redirect the old URLs
findings.what: 2 known legacy URL(s) need permanent redirects (301) onto the current IA. Examples: /old-services/, /book-a-call/
findings.why: Without 301s, bookmarks, social posts and AI-answer citations become dead ends, and Google drops the URLs without passing value on.
findings.fix: Add a redirects file (or platform equivalent) with permanent 301s, one line per old URL. Keep it at least a year.

findings.title: Titles, descriptions, headings
findings.what: Crawled pages have titles, meta descriptions, and a single H1.
findings.why: This is the technical baseline most consultancy sites still miss.
findings.fix: Keep the pattern as new pages are added.

findings.title: Add an Organization (or ProfessionalService) to the schema
findings.what: JSON-LD is present (WebSite) but there is no Organization / ProfessionalService entity for the business itself.
findings.why: Without an organisation entity, engines may treat the brand as a topic or confuse it with namesakes. AI assistants invent descriptions when the entity is unclear.
findings.fix: Add ProfessionalService (or Organization) with name, legalName ("Northline Advisory Ltd"), url, address, founder, sameAs profile links, and knowsAbout.

findings.title: A proper social preview image
findings.what: og:image is set but twitter:card is "summary" (prefer summary_large_image with a 1200×630 image).
findings.why: Shared links on LinkedIn otherwise show a cropped logo or empty preview.
findings.fix: Create one 1200×630 image (logo + headline), set as default og:image, use summary_large_image.

findings.title: The contact form posts to mailto:
findings.what: Found mailto form action(s): https://staging.northline.example/ → mailto:hello@northline.example
findings.why: This is a conversion issue more than an SEO one, but it is the page SEO work sends people to. On many phones and locked-down work machines, mailto does nothing.
findings.fix: Post to a real form endpoint (HubSpot, Formspree, etc.) and show the email address as plain-text fallback.

findings.title: Search demand and content fit
findings.what: Configured focus themes/keywords to validate with search-volume data: incident review, observability advisory.
findings.why: Category keywords often have tiny demand for advisory businesses; buyers search symptoms or ask AI assistants.
findings.fix: Pull monthly volumes (DataForSEO / Ads Keyword Planner) for the configured markets, then write problem-led pages that open with a two-sentence direct answer and link to the matching service.

agentAction.notes: Fill volumes via keyword collector or agent research, then prioritise content.

findings.title: How AI search sees the brand (manual / API pass)
findings.what: Live ChatGPT / Perplexity / AI Overview answers were not auto-fetched in this run. Use the configured questions.
findings.why: Assistants still describe brands from old crawls; redirects and llms.txt decide how fast that updates.
findings.fix: Ask each question with web search enabled, record citations, and compare to the intended positioning. Re-run 2–4 weeks after major changes.

agentAction.notes: Fill GEO answers into the report

findings.title: Win the brand search on purpose
findings.what: Brand strings to verify in Google (GB): Northline. Known namesakes/competitors: https://other-northline.example/.
findings.why: Prospects who hear the name will search it. They need to land on the right domain, not a namesake.
findings.fix: Put brand + place + category together in the home title or first paragraph. Align LinkedIn, Google Business Profile, and other sameAs profiles on the exact name and URL.
